nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 12          |
-------------------------------


##You wake to the hum.##

A low, electric drone that vibrates through the floor, through the walls,
through the bones of your skull.# It is the first thing you are aware of, before the pain,
before the cold, before the memory of what happened.##

You are lying on your side on a smooth metal floor, your mouth tasting of copper and ozone,
your head feeling like it has been split open and reassembled by someone who did not care
about the instruction manual.##

$c<<Ow.>>#

$CYou open your eyes.##

Gray. Everything is gray. Gray walls, gray ceiling, a narrow rectangular space,#
perhaps three meters by two, lit by a strip of sickly white light recessed into the ceiling.#
No windows, no furniture. Just the floor, the walls, and you.##

You sit up slowly, every muscle protesting, and that is when you see the barrier.##

Where a door should be, there is...# nothing. An opening.#
But the air in that opening $mshimmers$C, a faint translucent curtain of rippling light,
like heat haze made solid.# You reach toward it instinctively and...#

$WPAIN.$C#

A jolt of pure agony shoots up your arm, locking every muscle from wrist to shoulder,#
and you stumble backward, gasping, cradling your hand against your chest.##

$c<<Force field. I'm behind a force field. In a cell.>>#

$CThe last thing you remember is the golden shield...# collapsing?##
The vertigo, the blackness.# And before that, someone carrying you, drab streets, blank faces...##

$c<<They caught us.>>$C

dialogues.precomment:
You drag yourself to the barrier and peer through the shimmer.#
The corridor beyond is narrow and featureless, lined with identical cells on both sides.
dialogues.line:
KRISS!# Kriss, you're awake! Oh thank the stars you're awake!#
I thought you were dead! You were so still! You wouldn't move and I kept calling and calling...
dialogues.comment:
Smiurl's voice, high and frantic, hits you from one of the cells directly across from yours.#
You can see him pressed against his own barrier, careful not to touch it,
his skin flickering a rapid, panicked amber.

dialogues.line: I'm okay, Smiurl. I'm okay.
dialogues.comment: You are not okay, but he does not need to know that.

dialogues.precomment: From the cell beside Smiurl's, Corolla's voice cuts through like a blade.
dialogues.line:
About time.# We've been stuck in these boxes for hours.#
They took our weapons. They took $Weverything$R.
dialogues.comment:
Her voice is controlled, but you can hear the fury simmering beneath every syllable.#
She is pacing, three steps forward, three steps back, a caged predator.

dialogues.line: But when I get my hands free, I swear on my father's grave...
dialogues.comment: She stops herself, her jaw tightening. She does not finish the sentence.

dialogues.precomment: A voice comes from the cell on your left.
dialogues.line: The shield... drained us. Efeliah and I.# Our minds are...# quiet.
dialogues.comment: Math sounds like he has aged ten years.

dialogues.line: I cannot reach beyond these walls. Not yet. I need time to recover.

replies.line: "What happened out there? At the shield?"
"Forget the shield. How do we get out of here?"

dialogues.line:
You went through it.# I was holding on to you and I still cannot tell you how.##
Then the light went out of the world, and so did we.
dialogues.comment:
He reports it the way a man reports something he watched happen
and does not believe he watched.

dialogues.line:
I was already unconscious, and my mind recorded it anyway.#
A pulse of psychic energy, enormous.# I think you shorted the shield out.
dialogues.comment: A pause, and then, quieter:

dialogues.line: I do not think it was enough to destroy it.
And then somebody scraped us up off the ground and carried us in here.
dialogues.comment: She says it flatly, the way you would read out a list.

dialogues.line:
I said we should not come!# I said it!# A cursed city, I said!##
And now we are going to die down here and nobody will ever know it.
dialogues.comment: Nobody argues with him. That is the worst part.

dialogues.precomment:
You put your palm flat against the wall beside the opening.#
Smooth, seamless, cold.
dialogues.line:
Not through that.# The walls are solid and the doorway is not a doorway.##
Whatever that curtain is, it does not care how hard you hit it.

It is an electric field.# Whoever touches it takes a shock.#
I can promise you that much.
dialogues.comment:
You cradle your wrist, which is still not entirely on speaking terms with you,
and say nothing.##

It occurs to you, slowly, that Math knows what an electric field is.#
Nobody at Seer's Rock ever mentioned a wire.# The decay of this planet
is beginning to show you its seams.

dialogues.precomment:
Efeliah must be in the other cell beside yours.# You cannot see her directly;
her mind voice reaches you, thin and strained, like silk stretched to its limit.
dialogues.line:
There are minds here. So many minds.# But they are... dim.#
Smothered, like candle flames under glass.

dialogues.precomment:
You look to the cell beside Smiurl's, opposite from Corolla's.# Theo.

He is sitting in front of the barrier, legs and arms folded,#
his massive frame perfectly still, his eyes fixed.#

He has not said a word.
dialogues.line: Theo? You alright?
dialogues.comment:
He does not answer. He does not even look at you.#
His eyes are moving, slowly, methodically, following something you cannot see.#

Whatever he's doing, he's clearly up to something.

nodes.text:
Time passes.# You have no way to measure it:
minutes or hours swallowed by the hum and the bleached light.##

And then you hear it.# Footsteps.##

Slow and metronomic, soon enough a figure rounds the corner of the corridor.##

A guard. A woman, perhaps thirty, in a grayish uniform that hangs loose on her frame.#
Her face...## blank.##

Empty. Wiped clean.# Her eyes are open, but there is no one behind them.#
Across her forehead, a thin $Wmetal headband$C, its surface dull and featureless,
except for two small nodes at the temples that pulse with a faint, rhythmic light.##

nodes.recap: the guard walks the corridor: call out, study the band, or stay quiet [DECISION: replies]
nodes.text:
She has not looked at any of you yet.##

She is coming.##

dialogues.precomment: Math's voice comes low and flat from the cell on your left.
dialogues.line:
She is not a machine.# I am dulled and half blind tonight
and I can still tell you that much.##
Whatever has been done to her, the mind inside there is a human mind.
dialogues.comment: He does not sound comforted by that, and neither are you.

replies.line: Watch the band on her head instead.
Say nothing, and let her pass.

dialogues.comment:
You call to her through the shimmer.# You ask her name.##

Her stride does not change by so much as a fraction.# Not a flinch,#
not a glance, not the smallest hitch anywhere in her.# Whatever the word
for what she is doing is, it is not ignoring you.##

dialogues.precomment:
You keep your eyes on the circlet, on the dull metal and the small steady
pulse of it, and you try to fix the shape of the thing in your memory.
dialogues.line:
I would want a longer look at that thing than she will give us.#
And I am too dulled, tonight, to take one.

dialogues.comment:
So you do the only thing left to do, which is nothing at all.##

You stand at the edge of your cell, just back from the shimmer,# and you watch
her come.##

nodes.text:
She walks the corridor slowly, methodically, her eyes sweeping each cell
with the precision of a security camera, but there is no recognition in them,#
no curiosity, no threat assessment, just the flat, mechanical scan of a machine
performing a routine.##

She passes your cell. Your eyes meet.##

Nothing. Less than nothing.# You have looked into the eyes of animals with way more presence.#

You wonder if there is a person in there...## still.##

She continues to the end of the corridor, turns with mechanical precision,#
and walks back the way she came. Gone.##

Silence returns, and the hum fills the void.##

$g<<There is a mind in there. I can feel the outline of it.#
But the inside is...# static. White noise where a person should be.>>$C#

Efeliah's telepathic voice cracks.#

$g<<Every one of them. Every guard, every patrol, all of them still in there.#
And no one can hear them.>>$C##

You look at Theo.##

For the first time since you woke up, his expression has changed.#
His jaw is set, his eyes are hard, and the calm, patient observation
has been replaced by something colder.###

Steeled determination.

nodes.recap: the cells: what Kriss does while Theo prepares [DECISION: replies]
nodes.text:
Nobody says anything for a while.##

Theo has not moved from the front of his cell.# The expression is still there,
the hard one, and his eyes are still travelling the corridor, slowly,
measuring something none of the rest of you can see.##

Math and Efeliah look at each other across the width of the passage, and say
nothing at all.# You find yourself straining to hear it, the thing that must be
passing between them,# and for half a second you would swear that you almost do.##

dialogues.precomment: Smiurl's light has gone a thin, unhappy blue.
dialogues.line: Why is he doing that?# Why is nobody saying anything about it?

replies.line: Ask Corolla what Theo is planning.
Ask Math and Efeliah to bring the guard back here.

dialogues.precomment:
You catch Corolla's eye across the corridor
and tip your head toward Theo's cell.
dialogues.line: Don't look at me.# I have no idea what he intends to do.
dialogues.comment:
She does not look worried, though, and somehow that is worse.#
Whatever it is, she has already decided to let him do it.

dialogues.precomment: The two telepaths confer, briefly, without a sound.
dialogues.line:
Perhaps.# His mind is hypnotized, and a hypnotized mind is not easy to speak to.##
But we can try.
dialogues.comment: Efeliah closes her eyes. A moment later, so does Math.

You sit down with your back against the wall, and you settle in to watch him.##

He does not blink more than a man has to.# He does not shift his weight.##

He simply waits, and because he waits, so do the rest of you.##

nodes.text:
Then Theo moves.##

No word.# No warning.# He rises and sets himself at the edge of his barrier,#
his right arm drawn back, his eyes fixed on the mouth of the corridor.##

$Y"Theo?# Theo, what are you..."$C# Smiurl's voice climbs toward panic.##

Corolla is already at the front of her cell, gripping the doorframe, knuckles white.#
She has understood.# You can see it in her face,# and you can see that she knows
there is no stopping him now.##

$c<<Theo, whatever this is...>>##

$CFootsteps.###

Distant, then not: the mechanical drumbeat of a single pair of boots.# Closer.# Closer.

The guard rounds the corner.##

A man this time, broad-shouldered, slack-jawed, dead-eyed, the headband pulsing
at his temples.# He carries a short metal baton at his hip, his footsteps
perfectly even, mechanical, unstoppable.##

He passes Smiurl's cell, Corolla's, yours.# He reaches Theo's.##

Theo $Wmoves$C.###

One arm punches THROUGH the barrier!##

The sound that comes out of Theo is not human, a roar ripped from somewhere
deeper than the lungs, deeper than the chest, a sound of pure, burning, defiant agony
as the force field tears into his flesh.##

His hand closes around the guard's throat.##

The guard does not react, does not flinch, does not scream.#
His dead eyes stare at Theo as if observing a mildly unusual weather pattern.##

And Theo does not pull him out.# He drives him $Win$C.###

With one savage heave he hauls the guard bodily into the barrier,#
forcing a whole living body into a field built to turn back a fingertip.##

$WLIGHT.$C###

A blinding arc of electricity erupts from the point of contact, blue-white fire
screaming through the conduit, branching like lightning, following every seam,
every groove, racing through the walls, the ceiling, the floor.##

Every barrier in the corridor $Wshrieks$C, a sound like tearing metal,
like a thousand tuning forks shattering at once, and the shimmering curtains
flicker, spasm, and die.##

But Theo does not let go.##

The current is flowing $Wthrough$C him. You can see it.#
His entire body is rigid, every muscle locked, his teeth bared, his eyes wide and white,#
blue sparks dancing across his skin, his hair standing on end.##

His arm is still through the space where the barrier was, his hand still clamped
around the guard's throat. The guard has gone limp, and the headband is glowing
cherry-red.##

$c"LET GO!# THEO, LET GO!"$C#

He can't. The current has him, and his muscles are not his own.##

And then, with a sound like a gunshot, the conduit blows.##

Darkness, absolute, as the ceiling light dies with the barriers.##

A heavy thud, then another...# then silence.###

The hum is gone.

Emergency lighting flickers on, dim red, barely enough to see.##

You are on your feet before you know it, stumbling through the dead barrier frame,#
your bare feet hitting cold corridor metal.# Theo is lying face-down on the floor,#
and the guard is crumpled against the far wall, motionless.##

You drop to your knees beside Theo.#

$c"Theo!"$C#

His skin is hot. Not warm. $WHot$C, like touching a radiator,#
and the smell of singed hair fills the corridor.# Black marks trace branching lines
up his forearm, across his shoulder, like a diagram of the current's path
burned into his flesh.##

He is not moving.##

Corolla is beside you in an instant, her hands steady as she presses
two fingers to his throat. Her face says everything her mouth will not.##

One second.# Two.# Three.###

$R"Pulse."$C#

She breathes the word like a prayer.##

Smiurl makes a sound that is half sob, half laugh, his skin flooding
with golden light, bright enough to cast shadows in the red-lit corridor.##

Theo's eyes open. He blinks, once, twice, looks up at the cluster of faces
above him, and his lips crack into the faintest ghost of a smile.##

$B"Why the long face."$C##

Corolla echoes Smiurl with a noise somewhere between a laugh and a sob,#
and punches him in the shoulder. Hard.##

$R"Don't you $Wever$R do that again."$C#

Her eyes are bright, and she turns away before anyone can see them clearly.

Math emerges from his cell, leaning heavily against the doorframe,#
and Efeliah follows, one hand on the wall for support.#
She looks at Theo and closes her eyes.##

$c"You beautiful, stubborn, impossible absolute unit of a man!"$C# you exclaim, a grin ear to ear.#

Theo sits up, winces, and looks at the burn marks on his arm
with detached curiosity.##

$B"Could have been worse."$C##

$c"He just electrocuted himself on purpose and his review is
'could have been worse.'# I will never understand this man."#

$CThe corridor stretches ahead of you, dim and silent under the emergency lights.#
The barriers are dead, your cells are open, but you are still deep inside whatever
this building is, and somewhere beyond the heavy door at the far end of the corridor
there are more cells, more prisoners, more people buried alive behind static and silence.

You help Theo to his feet. He sways once, steadies, and stands,#
and the group moves cautiously down the corridor under the dim red emergency lights,#
the downed guard slumped against the wall behind you.#

Ahead, the corridor widens into a larger cellblock.#
More cells line both walls, their barriers still $Mactive$C, still humming,#
fed by a different circuit than the one Theo destroyed, and behind the shimmering
curtains you can see figures, motionless, staring.##

A metal storage alcove is set into the left wall, and the corridor terminates
at a heavy sealed door with a control panel beside it.


$D[Type an action at the prompt. Press TAB for help.]$C

actions.answer:
The cellblock stretches before you under red emergency light.
Active barriers hum in cells on both sides.
There is a storage alcove to the left, a control panel by the far door,
and the downed guard behind you.

objects.answer:
Behind the active barriers, figures sit or stand in perfect stillness,
men and women, young and old, each wearing a metal headband, each staring at nothing.
One woman is mouthing words silently, over and over,
like a prayer no one taught her to forget.

You trace the corridor walls carefully.
The same metal conduit grooves run here, but these connect to a separate circuit:
a control panel mounted beside the sealed door at the far end.
It has a row of switches and a status display still glowing faint green.

The panel is simple, military-functional.
A row of heavy switches labeled in faded text you cannot read,
and a central override lever marked in red.
The status display shows a grid of cell numbers, each glowing green. Active. All of them.

condition.refusal: I should look around more carefully first. There has to be a way to control these barriers.

objects.answer:
The guard is unconscious, slumped at an awkward angle.
The headband on his forehead is cracked, its temple nodes dark and dead.
Beneath it, the skin is red and blistered.
Up close, his face looks... younger than you thought. Softer.
As if something has relaxed in the muscles now that the signal is gone.

You examine the cracked headband on the guard's forehead.
It is warm to the touch, lightweight, with two small nodes at the temples
connected by a thin metal strip.
The craftsmanship is ancient: precise but worn.
A tiny crystal is set into each node, one of them fractured from the surge.

The storage alcove contains standard-issue equipment: gray uniforms, restraint bands,
and, buried under a pile of confiscated belongings, a medical kit.
Old but intact, with bandages, salve, and a vial of something that smells sharply antiseptic.

The door is solid metal, sealed shut.
A heavy-duty mechanism that will not yield to force.
The control panel beside it seems to govern both the cell barriers and the door lock.

actions.answer: You are not sure what to use, or on what.

objects.answer:
You grip the red override lever and pull. It resists for a moment, then gives.

The effect is immediate. Every barrier in the cellblock dies at once,
the shimmer collapsing like a held breath finally released.
The status display flickers from green to dark, cell by cell, like stars going out.
The sealed door at the far end clicks and swings ajar.

The hum is gone. Replaced by something almost worse: silence.
And then, slowly, the sound of people stirring
who have not moved of their own will in a very long time.

condition.refusal: I need to find whatever controls these barriers first.
I have nothing to treat that with.# I would need to find a kit first.

objects.answer:
You dig the medical kit out and set to work on Theo's arm.
He watches you do it with the mild interest of a man observing
someone else's hobby, and offers no reaction as you clean
the branching burns and wind the bandage tight.

$B"You missed a spot."$y# He says it when you finish. He did not.

It will not undo what the current did to him, but the salve draws
the worst of the heat from the wound, and the bandage will hold.
It is something.

actions.answer: There is no time for careful work, but Theo's burned arm is the worst of it.

condition.refusal: I have nothing to treat that with.# I would need to find a kit first.

objects.answer:
You dig the medical kit out and set to work on Theo's arm.
He watches you do it with the mild interest of a man observing
someone else's hobby, and offers no reaction as you clean
the branching burns and wind the bandage tight.

$B"You missed a spot."$y# He says it when you finish. He did not.

It will not undo what the current did to him, but the salve draws
the worst of the heat from the wound, and the bandage will hold.
It is something.

actions.answer: You want to help, but you need to figure out how first.

condition.refusal: The barriers are still active. I need to find a way to shut them down first.

actions.answer: Nobody here is in any state to talk.

objects.answer:
You call out to the figures behind the barriers. Nothing. Not a flinch. Not a blink.
One man's lips are moving, but no sound comes out.
Their eyes pass over you as if you are furniture.
The guard is unconscious. He does not respond.

actions.answer: You look around, but nothing useful catches your eye to take.

objects.answer:
You take the guard's baton. It is heavier than it looks:
solid metal with a rubberized grip. Not a sword, but better than bare hands.

You pry the cracked headband from the guard's forehead and pocket it.
The crystal nodes are dark. Dead technology, for now.
But Math might want to examine it.

You grab the medical kit from the storage alcove.
Old but intact, with bandages, salve, and antiseptic.

actions.answer: Where? The only way forward is through the sealed door at the end.

condition.refusal: I am not leaving these people behind those barriers.

actions.answer:
You stand in the dim red light, listening to the hum of active barriers
and the sound of your own breathing.
Somewhere deeper in the complex, something mechanical clicks at regular intervals.
Time is not on your side.

dialogues.precomment:
The freed prisoners stir like sleepwalkers. Most sit where they are,#
blinking, confused, the headbands dark and lifeless on their foreheads.#
Some pull at the bands with trembling hands, others simply stare.##

But one figure stands.##

He is wiry, medium height, with close-cropped hair and a jaw-length scar
that pulls the left side of his mouth into a permanent half-grimace.#
His eyes are sharp and alert, and $Whe is not wearing a headband.$C##

He steps out of his cell and looks at your group with the expression of a man
who has been waiting for something impossible and just watched it walk through the door.
dialogues.line: You.# You brought the barrier down.
dialogues.comment:
His voice is rough, cracked from disuse, but underneath the rasp
there is something fierce, something unbroken.

replies.line: "Him, mostly. He put his arm through it."

dialogues.precomment:
You gesture at Theo, who is leaning against the wall,#
cradling his burned arm with quiet stoicism.##

The man looks at Theo, taking in the burn marks, the size of him,
the fact that he is standing at all.
dialogues.line: Then he has my respect. And my thanks.
dialogues.comment: He turns back to you and studies your face.

dialogues.line:
My name is Riff.# I lead what is left of the resistance in this city,#
or I did, before they caught me.
dialogues.comment: He gestures at the confused, stumbling figures around him.

dialogues.line:
These people were free once. Fighters, thinkers, anyone who would not bend.#
Joe took them, put the bands on them, added them to his collection.
dialogues.comment: The bitterness in his voice could etch glass.

dialogues.line: How many of you are left? Uncontrolled?
dialogues.comment:
Corolla has her arms crossed, measuring Riff
the way she measures everything: quickly, thoroughly, and without apparent sentiment.

dialogues.line:
A handful, hidden in the service tunnels beneath the city.#
We have been fighting Joe for...# I have lost track. Months. Years, maybe.#
Hard to tell in a city where the sky is a lie.
dialogues.comment:
He looks at the ceiling,
as if he can see through it to the golden illusion above.

nodes.recap: Riff exposition about Joe and Projector

dialogues.line: Who is Joe? What is he using to do all this?

dialogues.precomment: Riff's jaw tightens, and the scar pulls white.
dialogues.line:
Joe.# Self-proclaimed Tyrant of Ayonn.# That is what he calls himself. Tyrant.#
Not king, not leader.# $WTyrant$y, as if it is something to be proud of.
dialogues.comment: He spits the word like poison.

dialogues.line:
He controls the city through a machine, ancient technology.#
It sits in the Municipal building, that ugly tower in the center of the city,#
and they call it the $WProjector$y.

The Projector does two things.# It generates the golden shield over the city,#
the illusion, the fear that keeps outsiders away.# And it generates the $Wsignal$y,#
the one that feeds those headbands, the one that erases people.
dialogues.comment: He taps his own bare forehead.

dialogues.line:
Control the Projector,# control the headbands.#
Control the headbands,# control the city.#
Every guard, every soldier, every worker: all puppets.#
One man, pulling all the strings.

dialogues.precomment:
Math has been listening with growing intensity,#
his bloodshot eyes suddenly alight with recognition.
dialogues.line:
A psychic amplification machine...# The Projector...#
This is the Master's work.
dialogues.comment: His voice is barely a whisper, reverent and horrified in equal measure.

dialogues.line:
The Memories speak of it, a device built to shield a community,#
to project mental energy across great distances.#
But it was never meant for...# $Wthis$m.
dialogues.comment: He looks physically ill.

dialogues.precomment:
Efeliah has been sitting quietly, her hands pressed to her temples,#
her breathing slow and deliberate, recovering.#
When she speaks, her voice still uncertain, but present.
dialogues.line:
If the Projector generates the signal...# then the Projector can end it.#
Those minds are not destroyed. They are $Wsuppressed$g.#
Disable the signal# and they wake up. All of them.

That is what we have been trying to do, for months.#
But the Municipal building is a fortress.#
Guards on every floor,# and a door on the top level that no weapon can force open.#
We have thrown everything at it, every assault, every scheme, every suicide run.
dialogues.comment:
He looks down at his hands.
They are shaking, not with fear, with exhaustion.

dialogues.line:
We lost good people.# A lot of good people.#
And every one we didn't, Joe put a headband on and sent back against us.
dialogues.comment: His voice is steady. But his eyes are not.

replies.line: "I am sorry. For all of them."

dialogues.precomment:
A heavy silence settles over the group.#
Corolla breaks it.
dialogues.line: About that door.# There must be a way to open it or get past it.

Top floor of the Municipal building, before the Projector room.#
That door that has no lock, no handle, no mechanism.# Maybe it only opens to the $Wmind$y.#
We have tried explosives, battering rams, fire.# Nothing. It does not even scratch.

A psi-lock.# It requires a psychic key.#
A mind equipped with either the needed knowledge or sufficient strength, or both.
dialogues.comment: He looks at Efeliah, and she looks back.

dialogues.line: We can do it. Together, when we have recovered.
dialogues.comment:
She says it simply, as a fact, and Riff stares at her
as if she has just promised to move the sun.

dialogues.precomment:
Riff looks at your group, really looks: the giant with the burned arm
who broke a force field with his bare hands, the dark-haired woman with murder in her eyes,
the two telepaths, drained but unbroken,#
the glowing dwarf who is somehow still here,# and you, a stranger from nowhere
who just happened to waltz through an impassable psychic shield.
dialogues.line: Who the hell are you people?
dialogues.comment:
For the first time, something cracks in his composure.#
Not despair, its opposite...##

Hope.

nodes.text:
Riff leads you through maintenance corridors no map would show,#
duct-lined passages behind walls, beneath floors, through the guts of a city
that was never designed for secrecy but has been made to serve it.##

He moves with the practiced ease of a man who knows every bolt, every hatch,#
every camera blind spot by heart, and the freed prisoners follow in a stumbling line,#
some supported by others, the headbands removed and discarded like dead insects.##

Three turns, two ladders, one long tunnel through dripping darkness,#
and you emerge into warmth.##

A wide, low-ceilinged room, underground, clearly.# Concrete walls hung
with salvaged blankets, mismatched furniture, a table covered in hand-drawn maps.#
Oil lanterns cast flickering orange light across the faces of a dozen people
who rise to their feet as Riff enters, their expressions shifting from alarm
to disbelief to joy.##

Rebels. Survivors. The last free minds in Ayonn.##

Riff grips the forearm of a woman who rushes forward, her eyes brimming.#
He squeezes once, nods, and that is all they need.##

The room comes alive.##

Someone finds food, bread and dried meat and a thin, sharp broth
that warms you from the inside out.# You eat ravenously, barely tasting it,#
and it is the best thing you have ever put in your mouth.##

nodes.recap: the free night [DECISION: choice hub] - four vignettes in any order, all four open the plan
nodes.text:
The room settles into something that is almost peace.##

You have an hour, maybe two, before anybody starts saying the word tomorrow.
nodes.alttext: The lanterns burn on, and the room is still awake around you.

choices.desc: Sit with Efeliah while she works on Theo's arm.
Watch Smiurl in the corner with the rebel children.
Go over to the map table, where Corolla and Riff are.
Say the thing you have been turning over since the cells.

nodes.text:
Efeliah sits beside Theo, her hands gentle on his burned arm, her brow furrowed
in concentration as she channels what little psychic energy she has recovered
into easing the pain.# Theo watches her work with an expression of faint,
grudging gratitude.##

You sit down near them, and you do not interrupt.##

In the corner, Smiurl has attracted a small cluster of rebel children.##

His skin is cycling through soft, gentle colors, lavender, warm gold,
a shy seafoam green, and the children are reaching out to touch his arm,#
giggling, pulling their hands back and then reaching again.# He is telling them
something, gesturing wildly, and they are rapt.# For a moment, in the orange
lamplight, he is not afraid.##

nodes.recap: the map table, and what Riff has lost [DECISION: replies]
nodes.text:
Corolla and Riff are bent over the map table, heads close together.#
She is pointing at something, and he is shaking his head. She insists.#
He pauses, looks at her with narrowed eyes, then nods, slowly.#
Something has just been decided.##

dialogues.precomment:
Corolla straightens, taps the map once more with two fingers,
and goes off to see what the rebels can spare in the way of a blade.##

Riff stays where he is, both hands flat on the table, looking down at a city
he has drawn from memory more times than he can possibly remember.
dialogues.line:
We had wives.# Children.# Houses with doors that locked from the inside.##
Joe took all of it, one piece at a time.
dialogues.comment: He does not look up while he says it.

dialogues.line:
And the taking is not the worst of it.# Before he found the signal
there was still a light out there somewhere, small, but there.##
Now there is not even that.
We have lost everything.# Even the hope of it.
dialogues.comment: He stops.# His throat works, once.

replies.line: "You are still fighting. That is not nothing."
"Then we will bring you back something better."

dialogues.line: Hope.# I had forgotten I was allowed to want it.
dialogues.comment:
Math has come to stand at his shoulder without anybody noticing him do it,
and Efeliah is already there on the other side.# Neither of them says a word.##

Riff lets out a breath that has clearly been inside him a long time.##

nodes.text:
Math sits apart, cross-legged, eyes closed, his lips moving silently,
reciting, perhaps, the Master's Memories, drawing strength from ancient words
against a very modern darkness.##

You watch him for a while, and you leave him to it.##

nodes.recap: Kriss proposes the diversion, and the objections [DECISION: replies]
nodes.text:
You have been holding it since the cells, turning it over,#
looking for the place where it comes apart in your hands.##

It has not come apart yet.# So you say it out loud.##

dialogues.precomment:
The room goes quiet in the particular way a room goes quiet when everybody
in it has decided to pretend they were not listening.
dialogues.line:
Let me be sure I have understood.# That is your plan?##
Perhaps you had better say it to me again.

It is surprisingly simple.# Your people pull the municipal guard to the front
of that building,# we go in from the side,# we find the machine,#
we shut it off.# Everything after that takes care of itself.
dialogues.comment:
You say it to all of them, one at a time, and it sounds better out loud
than it has any right to.

dialogues.line: You said it yourself.# It is too simple.
dialogues.comment: He is not remotely infected by your optimism.

dialogues.line:
You have to admit that he is right.# You have not the faintest idea where the
Municipal building is, nor where this Projector sits inside it, nor how anybody
turns such a thing off once they have found it.##
And suppose you manage all three.# How do we come out again?#
This Joe will have men who follow him without a band on their heads.
dialogues.comment: Riff nods slowly. He does not enjoy agreeing with her.

replies.line: "I know that we will manage it."
"Because it is the right thing to do."

dialogues.precomment:
You shift your weight from one foot to the other, and your hands go looking
for the pommel of a sword that is locked in a cupboard somewhere in this city.##

How could anybody walk out and leave this place, and these people, in the hands
of a man like that?# You say so, and you say the rest of it too, with all the
conviction you can put into your voice, which turns out to be a great deal more
than you expected to find in there.
dialogues.line: You do not intend to stake a matter of life and death on a feeling.
dialogues.comment: It is not quite a question.

dialogues.line:
It is more than a feeling.# I cannot explain it.#
It is as though I can feel that this is the thing I am meant to do.##
The same as when I decided I would walk all the way here.#
Or when I climbed your Rock.
dialogues.comment: They look at you for a long moment, and nobody says anything at all.

nodes.recap: Efeliah's probe and the vote [DECISION: replies]

dialogues.precomment: Efeliah has not taken her eyes off you since you started talking.
dialogues.line: But there is something else. Isn't there.

replies.line: "I want to see the Projector. I want to know what it is."
"I am curious. More than curious. And I cannot say why."

dialogues.line: ...and you think that it may answer one or two of your questions.
dialogues.comment:
She finishes the sentence before you can get to the end of it yourself.##

You admit that yes, that is more or less it.

dialogues.line: I have a vague presentiment about that, as it happens.
dialogues.comment: She does not explain it, and you do not ask.

dialogues.line:
I am in.# I vote for Kriss's plan, whatever it turns out to be.##
Who else?
Naturally, I am coming with you.
dialogues.comment: No hesitation at all, which from Math is practically a shout.

dialogues.precomment: A small voice, from somewhere near the floor.
dialogues.line: Smiurl is ready to fight.
dialogues.comment:
He says it in the third person, which he only ever does when he is terrified,#
and he glitters faintly while he says it.# His friends stare at him.#
Nobody expected that, least of all him.

dialogues.line: I do not fear these automata.

dialogues.precomment:
Corolla looks at the lot of them, half surprised and half entertained,
and shrugs.
dialogues.line: Well then. It is decided.## Provided...
dialogues.comment: She looks at Riff.# Riff looks back at her with a strange light in his eyes.

dialogues.line: In truth, I do not believe we have any other choice.
dialogues.comment: He says it with resignation, and he is smiling while he says it.##

nodes.text:
You lean your back against the concrete wall.# The broth is warm in your belly,#
the lantern light is soft, and around you, people who were strangers an hour ago
are sharing food, tending wounds, speaking in low voices.##

Tomorrow, you go to war against a tyrant and his machine.#
Tomorrow, you storm a fortress and break down a door that has no lock.#
Tomorrow, everything changes.##

But tonight, just for tonight, you are free.##

You close your eyes.##
